Here are my findings.

## The production utility under review

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/Sha256.java`
- `Sha256.hex(String)` — UTF-8 bytes → `MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256")` → 64 lower-case hex via `String.format("%02x", b)` in a `StringBuilder` loop (lines 27-34). Private `digest()` helper wraps `getInstance` (lines 36-43).

## Duplicate SHA-256 / hex code found

There is one clear functional duplicate, in the test sources:

`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/AcceptanceBase.java`
- Line 9: `import java.security.MessageDigest;`
- Lines 282-294 (`protected static String sha256hex(String s)`): line 284 `byte[] digest = MessageDigest.getInstance("SHA-256").digest(s.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));` then line 287 `sb.append(String.format("%02x", b));` — byte-for-byte the same algorithm as `Sha256.hex`, just re-implemented in the test base.
- Lines 296-299 (`hexPrefixUpper`): line 298 `return sha256hex(s).substring(0, n).toUpperCase();` — mirrors the production `substring(...).toUpperCase(...)` derivations.

This is the acceptance-test oracle; it deliberately re-derives the hash independently of production code. `AcceptanceTest.java` (line 15, `coreIdentityKeyIsSha256Hex`) asserts the 64-hex shape against it.

No other SHA-256 or hand-rolled hex-encoding implementation exists in the repo. No `util` package hex/digest helper exists. No use of `toHexString`, `Hex`, or any encoder class anywhere.

## DigestUtils availability

- Not used anywhere in `src` — zero references to Apache `org.apache.commons.codec.digest.DigestUtils` or Spring's `org.springframework.util.DigestUtils`.
- Not declared directly in `/home/daniel/sandbox/pom.xml`. The pom has no explicit `commons-codec`, `guava`, or `spring-core` dependency entry (grep returned nothing).
- However it IS transitively on the classpath: the project inherits from `spring-boot-starter-parent` (pom line 15) and pulls in many Spring Boot starters (data-jpa, webmvc, security, actuator, etc.), which bring `commons-codec` in transitively. Confirmed present in the local Maven repo: `/home/daniel/.m2/repository/commons-codec/commons-codec` (many versions cached, latest 1.22.0). Spring's own `org.springframework.util.DigestUtils` ships with `spring-core` (also transitive via Boot).
- So `DigestUtils.sha256Hex(...)` (Apache Commons Codec) would very likely resolve without adding a dependency, though it is not explicitly declared — if you wanted it declared for safety it is not currently in the pom.

## All callers / references of `Sha256`

- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/OwnerCustomerCode.java:78` — `return Sha256.hex(normalizedTelephone + last).substring(0, 8).toUpperCase(Locale.ROOT);`
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/function/owner/AssignHousehold.java:31` — `return Sha256.hex(lastName + "|" + postcode).substring(0, 12);`

Those are the only two callers of `Sha256.hex(`. `AssignCustomerCode.java` and `OwnerCustomerCode.java` reference the behavior in Javadoc only. No test references the `Sha256` class directly (the tests use their own `sha256hex` in `AcceptanceBase`).
